history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: the Vasudeva Temple is the ancient Vishnu shrine standing ~10-30 m from (adjacent to / opposite) the Narsingh Temple in Lower Bazaar, Joshimath. It is counted among the 108 Divya Desams (Tiruppirudi), venerated by the Tamil Alvars. The presiding deity is a ~6-ft (2 m) black carved stone idol of Vasudeva in standing posture (Paramapurushan), with a dancing Ganesha to the left of the entrance (said to be one of only two such Ganeshas in India), Govardhana Vimanam, and separate shrines for Vinayaka, Brahma, Indira, Chandran, Navadurgas and Gauri Shankar. COORDINATE NOTE: the map geocoder's only 'Shri Vasudev Temple' pin is on Auli Road (30.53571, 79.5674), ~2.3 km south; however multiple independent sources (padayatra.com, tourindiawithdriver.com, visitor reviews) place the historic Vasudeva temple 10-30 m from the Narsingh temple in Lower Bazaar, and a place listing gives its location as NH 58 Joshimath at 30.556335, 79.566489 - coordinates set to the latter; the Auli Road pin may be a different or misplaced shrine (verify).

name: Vasudev Temple, Joshimath
town: Joshimath (Lower Bazaar, adjacent to Narsingh Temple)
town_description: Joshimath (Jyotirmath), in Chamoli district at ~1,890 m, is the first of Adi Shankaracharya's four maths and the winter seat of Badrinath. It is the gateway town for the Valley of Flowers, Hemkund Sahib and Badrinath, and a base for Auli skiing. The Narsingh and Vasudev temples stand together in the lower part of the town.
